premise.premise: The face map must detect and merge concurrent edits from two devices so that nothing on either device is ever lost.
premise.action: Premise fails CLINIC_REALITY (one practitioner, one device, one record; phone to iPad is sequential). Ship the reported-bug fix only: Save adopts the stroke autosave stamp, reads it after awaiting autosaves, and never overwrites local points on a 409 (e91bdaec3 + ac314b0fa, with c800e83bc's honest copy). Revert the widened two-device work (three-way merge, conflict-refresh machinery, version-checked autosave editor registry in 5654b2cd7/9520af4bb/ff0bf6700), which also removes F4's cause; if any of it is kept, F4 must be fixed before landing. Re-run the original draw -> autosave -> add point -> Save -> X check.

findings.source_line: P1 components/face-mapping/face-mapping-save.ts:57 — Press Save while a conflicting autosave is pending: the queue merges the remote point, then Save sends its pre-wait snapshot with the newly adopted stamp, deleting that point. Reproduced — stop Save when draining discovers a conflict; keep the payload and version from the same snapshot. (TM-07, DR-05)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: needs a second device to have written a remote point to the same face map while this device's autosave is pending; one practitioner writes one client's map on one device (CLINIC_REALITY).
findings.reason: Trigger is a conflicting autosave carrying another device's point; two devices writing one clinical record at once does not happen in a clinic (Shane 26 Sep: 'we never need two device sync ever').
findings.pattern: multi-device concurrent edit of one clinical record

findings.source_line: P1 lib/stroke-queue-send.ts:78 — Draw before the opening GET returns: `sync.live` is false, so the autosave writes unchecked and erases another device’s point. Reproduced — wait for authoritative synchronization and reconcile before writing; an unavailable stamp must not authorize an unchecked replacement. (TM-07, DR-01)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: the practitioner would have to draw before the opening GET returns AND a second device must have written the same map; both halves fail CLINIC_REALITY.
findings.reason: Human racing the opening load, and the only harm is erasing another device's point on the same record; if the load is realistically seconds on clinic wifi, the smallest guard is disabling the pen until loaded, never a sync protocol.
findings.pattern: a person acting inside a sub-second or few-second window

findings.source_line: P1 lib/stroke-queue-send.ts:85 — Close the editor while its checked autosave is pending: a genuine 409 is retried unchecked, deleting the other device’s point. Reproduced — retain the conflicting snapshot for reconciliation after reopening, preserving its version check. (TM-07, DR-06)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: a genuine 409 only arises when another device wrote the same map; the single-device close-while-autosaving path still saves (unchecked, as on main).
findings.reason: The data loss is 'deleting the other device's point'; it needs two devices on one record. Unchecked retry with no editor open is main's pre-branch behaviour for the single device, so nothing regresses for a real clinic.
findings.pattern: multi-device concurrent edit of one clinical record

findings.source_line: P1 lib/stroke-queue-send.ts:67 — Draw during photo A’s pending Save, then replace the displayed photo with B: the captured editor resumes using B’s shared refs and PUTs B’s map into A. Reproduced — bind asynchronous sends to a photo-specific editor lifetime and revalidate that identity after waiting. (TM-07, UI-04)
findings.clinic_scenario: Practitioner on the treatment-room iPad annotates photo A, presses Save on clinic wifi (Save waits on queued autosaves that retry with backoff for up to a minute), then moves on to photo B of the same client at normal pace; A's queued autosave resumes with the editor's shared refs and writes B's map onto A.
findings.reason: Branch-caused (editor registry and snapshot() introduced in ff0bf6700) and one device misfiling its own clinical record; fix is to bind the send to the photo's editor lifetime, or drop the registry by reverting the widened autosave-check work per the premise action.
findings.demonstrated: Reviewer reproduced it. Traced path: lib/stroke-queue-send.ts sendStrokeSave awaits editor.whenNotSaving(), then sends editor.snapshot(); the editor registered for photo A (added in ff0bf6700) reads the modal's shared refs, which now hold B's map, and PUTs /api/photos/A/face-mapping. The system supplies the delay, not a human racing it.

findings.source_line: P1 components/face-mapping/face-mapping-conflict.ts:99 — Switch from A to B while A’s autosave conflict GET is pending: its callback merges A’s points into B’s canvas and replaces B’s synchronization state. Reproduced — invalidate callbacks on photo change/unmount and reject results from an obsolete editor lifetime. (TM-07, DR-05)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: the path starts from A's autosave conflict GET, which only fires after a genuine 409 from another device writing the same map.
findings.reason: Looks single-device (wrong-photo merge) but can only start from a two-device conflict callback; the pattern names this exact case (tiy3q r3 F5).
findings.pattern: multi-device concurrent edit of one clinical record

findings.source_line: P1 components/face-mapping/face-mapping-save.ts:83 — Both devices change a dose; a stroke drawn during conflict refresh resumes automatically and persists the locally chosen dose before the practitioner reviews the warning. Reproduced: remote 8 units became 6 despite “Check the map and press Save again” — pause autosaves on unresolved conflicts until explicit review and Save. (TM-07, UI-07, H-U0)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: requires both devices to change the same point's dose on one client's face map at once; the treating practitioner alone records doses in the room (CLINIC_REALITY, confirmed by Shane).
findings.reason: Two-device concurrent edit of one clinical record, the premise Shane rejected on 26 Sep; not a prescribing-pathway safety gate, it is conflict-resolution UX for a scenario that does not occur.
findings.pattern: multi-device concurrent edit of one clinical record

findings.source_line: P1 pages/api/photos/[photoId]/face-mapping.ts:201 — Two overlapping ordinary checked saves read the same version, pass the separate check, and both return 200; the last update replaces the first. Reproduced through the real handler with controlled database doubles; the actual SQL update has no version predicate. Pre-existing, but required by this bead’s promise — make comparison and update atomic, returning 409 to the losing writer. (DR-01, TM-07)
findings.clinic_scenario: none: two overlapping checked saves of the same face map need two writers on one record at the same moment.
findings.reason: Reviewer itself says pre-existing; server-side atomic version check only matters for two concurrent writers on one clinical record, which the clinic never has. Single-device saves are serialised by the branch's wait-for-autosaves.
findings.pattern: multi-device concurrent edit of one clinical record
